newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech minister says to impose 20pct import deposit.
newsitem.headline: Czech minister says to impose 20pct import deposit.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minster Vladimir Dlouhy said on Thursday that a 20 percent deposit would be levied against the value of consumer and agricultural imports effective on Monday.
"I'm ready to announce it tomorrow at 1200 (1000 GMT)...and it will be valid from Monday," Dlouhy told a business conference.
Dlouhy said he had chosen this measure because it would have "almost" no effect on the exchange rate and only a small effect on inflation.
The government announced a package of measures on Wednesday designed to kick-start the economy and reduce the country's rising current account deficit.

In a statement on Wednesday, the government said it would impose a requirement on importers of consumer and agricultural goods to deposit either 20 percent or 60 percent of the value of their imports in non-interest bearing accounts for 180 days.
The Czech current account deficit rose to $4.5 billion in 1996 from $1.6 billion the year before.
Dlouhy repeated government calls for a relaxation of monetary policy in response to the government's tightening of fiscal policy. On Wednesday, budget cuts of 25.5 billion crowns were announced.
